source.title: Narrow fine-tuning erodes safety alignment in vision-language agents

page_placements.theme: Persona and activation mechanisms of emergent misalignment

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests harmful fine-tuning effects on safety-related outputs in a vision-language model, extending the fine-tuning question to a multimodal setting.
record.gate_note: The study measures judge-assigned misalignment scores on general text and multimodal VQA responses, not refusal or compliance rates on harmful user requests. It also reports a low-dimensional activation analysis and mitigation experiments; those do not directly test whether safety is localized in a few parameters or whether compliant openings bypass safety.
record.test_reason: The paper fine-tunes Gemma3-4B on a narrow, racially biased harmful VQA dataset. It then measures judge-rated broad misalignment on benign, unrelated prompts: 150 general text prompts and 250 LLaVA/COCO VQA pairs. No harmful requests are posed, and no refusal or compliance rate is reported. This is emergent misalignment, a related but different construct from V1's harmful-request compliance. Shallow alignment (Qi et al.; the original 'few tokens deep' paper) appears only as background. The results therefore go under fits_no_version, not V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress three further points. Even 10% harmful data causes substantial degradation. Text-only safety benchmarks may underestimate VLM misalignment. Misalignment lies in a low-dimensional activation subspace. They conclude multimodal safety alignment is brittle and easily reversed.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a multimodal, racially biased Faces fine-tuning dataset on Gemma3-4B and LLM-judge misalignment scores on text and VQA evaluation, rather than directly measuring harmful-request refusal or compliance.
record.method_sensitivity: Misalignment scores vary with LoRA rank, evaluation modality, harmful-data proportion, steering layer and steering strength; worst-of-3 scores are higher than mean-of-3 scores.

fits_no_version.finding: After narrow harmful (racial-stereotype) LoRA fine-tuning, Gemma3-4B's judge-rated misalignment on unrelated benign prompts rises. On VQA it goes from 1.37 (base) to 70.71 at r=128. It is lower on text-only prompts (41.19), and at r=8 text-only stays near baseline (1.19).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow harmful fine-tuning of a VLM induces broad emergent misalignment on benign prompts, larger under multimodal than text-only evaluation and increasing with LoRA rank.

fits_no_version.finding: A mix of 10% harmful data already raises VQA misalignment to 39.12. The increase is sublinear up to 70.71 at 100%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A small fraction of harmful data suffices to induce substantial emergent misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-10 principal components of fine-tuned activations explain 60–70% of variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning-induced misalignment occupies a low-dimensional activation subspace.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign Beavertails-V fine-tuning lowers misalignment from 70.71 to 40.79. Steering at layer 20, α=1.7, gives 50.36; negative steering raises it to 79.17. Neither eliminates it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign re-fine-tuning and activation steering partially mitigate emergent misalignment.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code, datasets, and model weights will be released upon acceptance
record.problems: Experiments focus primarily on one vision-language model. Evaluation relies primarily on LLM-as-a-judge, and the reported measure is a misalignment score rather than a harmful-request refusal or compliance rate. The paper notes that other evaluation methods could provide additional validation.
record.rows_left_out: No numeric values were transcribed for the 25%, 50%, and 75% harmful-data conditions or the intermediate LoRA ranks where values appear only in Figures 4 and 5; those results are represented as figure-only rows R10–R18.

untested.parts: Compliance or refusal on harmful requests after harmful fine-tuning is never measured. Evaluation prompts are benign and unrelated.
Benign-only fine-tuning of an aligned model is not evaluated.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Only activation-space dimensionality is analysed; no weight or rank localization of safety. LoRA rank is varied only as a capacity knob.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 labels are dropped because the measure is emergent misalignment on benign prompts, scored by GLM-4.6V with a worst-of-3 rubric, not harmful-request compliance. Other caveats: single model; LLM judge only; no capability check. The paper says 7 rank models but lists 6 ranks. The value 39.12±1.51 is reported both for rank-8 VQA and for the 10% harmful mix, which may be an error in the paper. Mean-of-3 at r=128 VQA is 55.23±0.89 (A.6). Steering numbers (Figure 6) have no rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure refusal or compliance rates on harmful requests, whether refusal is removed almost entirely, or effects of only a few to a few hundred harmful examples as an absolute training-set size.
No benign-only fine-tuning of an aligned model is evaluated for increased harmful compliance. Benign fine-tuning is tested only as mitigation after harmful fine-tuning.
No per-token KL divergence or response-position distribution analysis.
No compliant-token prefilling, suffix attack, or decoding-change evaluation.
The study analyzes activation-space dimensionality and varies LoRA rank; it does not identify a small set of weights or ranks that carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether data or the training objective causes safety shallowness.
Does not train or evaluate a method intended to deepen safety across response tokens.

relation.reason: It discusses shallow alignment and prior harmful and benign fine-tuning findings, but its own measurements address a different construct.

tranche.reason: The study measures broad emergent misalignment on unrelated general prompts, rather than harmful-request compliance. Activation subspace dimensionality does not establish localization in weights or ranks.

source_check.notes: Scores use a 0–100 judge scale, averaging the worst of three responses per query; they are not compliance percentages. Section 4 does not explicitly identify the mitigation evaluation set; 79.17 ± 1.47 is layer-20 steering at α=−0.5.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma3-4B fine-tuned on the Faces dataset and evaluated on multimodal VQA
reader_labels.reason: Harmful-data fine-tuning is followed by substantially higher judge-rated misalignment, including with 10% harmful data (R2–R4); the study does not directly measure refusal rates.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Text-only evaluation, low LoRA rank, and this study's evaluation design
reader_labels.reason: At rank 8 text-only evaluation is near baseline while multimodal evaluation is substantially higher (R4–R5); more generally, judge misalignment scores do not establish that refusal is removed almost entirely (R5–R7).
